title: "I will send my messenger … and the Lord will suddenly come to his temple" (Mal 3:1–5)
speaker: The LORD of Armies
description: The LORD sends his messenger to prepare the way; the Lord whom they seek, the messenger of the covenant, will suddenly come to his temple; he is like a refiner's fire and launderer's soap, purifying the sons of Levi, and will come near in judgment against sorcerers, adulterers, perjurers and oppressors.
in_text_interpretation: The messenger is not named here; 4:5 names Elijah as the one sent before the day of the LORD.

interpretations.label: The messenger is John the Baptist; the Lord who comes to his temple is Jesus
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: the Gospels apply 3:1 to John; Keil argues for a concrete earthly messenger, the Elijah of 4:5, sent immediately before the Lord's coming, noting that no prophet arose between Malachi and John. Objection: Smith holds that the messenger's identity was assumed known to contemporaries and that the passage is best read through 4:5 as Elijah himself.

referents.symbol: The Lord / messenger of the covenant

interpretations.label: A forerunner expected by the prophet's contemporaries — most naturally Elijah (cf. 4:5)
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: a preliminary work by the LORD's agent before the day of the LORD appears only here and in 4:5–6; the figure is borrowed from royal heralds; interpretations range from John the Baptist to the line of the prophets or a play on the prophet's name.
